text:
sec-analyst: Heads up — we've had a spike in SIEM alerts for session_anomaly_high_concurrency starting ~1823456000. Roughly 220 alerts in the last hour. Most look like CI runner/service account noise rather than credential compromise. Thoughts on suppression vs rule refinement? :thinking:

marie: Can you paste a few raw events and the query that triggered the rule? want to validate pattern before we suppress anything.

olivia: Pasting two sanitized samples from the alert stream:
```
timestamp: 2026-03-19T14:12:05Z
principal: ci-build/infra-runner-7
ip: 10.4.12.7
session_id: s-9f3a
user_agent: gitlab-runner/14.2.0
auth_method: token
action: start_session

timestamp: 2026-03-19T14:12:17Z
principal: ci-build/infra-runner-7
ip: 10.4.12.7
session_id: s-9f3b
user_agent: gitlab-runner/14.2.0
auth_method: token
action: start_session
```
These are the ones that are flooding. Same principal, same ip, different session ids.

ashish: Ok pattern is clear. It's the CI orchestrator spawning many short sessions. Two options:
- exclude principals that match regex ci-build/.* from this specific high_concurrency rule (low risk)
- or require the rule to additionally check for distinct geoip or auth anomalies (eg. distinct public_ip_count > 3 in 5m) so legitimate lateral moves still alert

ben: I prefer not to blunt the rule entirely. Suggest: add a service_account exclusion whitelist AND tighten to distinct_ip_count >= 4 OR kms_decrypt_count > 0 within 5m. If someone is authenticating widely and also hitting KMS, escalate to P1.

sec-analyst: Agreed. Also propose a suppression cooldown: if a principal triggers X alerts within Y seconds and matches ci-runner UA, suppress duplicates for 10m but increment an aggregated metric we can chart. That way we don't lose visibility.

marie: Good call. Can you share the updated detection pseudocode so I can review?

ashish: Pseudocode suggestion:
```
if principal not match /^ci-build\// then
  if distinct_public_ip_count >= 4 in last 5m then alert P1
  else if kms_decrypt_count > 0 in last 5m then alert P1
  else if session_count > 50 in last 1m then alert P2
else
  suppress duplicate alerts for 10m and emit metric 'ci_session_burst'
end
```

olivia: +1 for emitting metric. I'll add a dashboard panel for ci_session_burst and a short-running histogram for frequency so SRE can spot unusual deviation.

deploy-bot: detection rule "session_anomaly_high_concurrency" updated in staging (rule id: 9032-stg) — ran tests against last 24h stream, suppressed ~180 noise alerts, flagged 3 distinct candidates for review.

ben: Nice. Can we also update the runbook to call out KMS usage as an escalation fork? if kms_decrypt_count > 0 then follow incident playbook A. Otherwise follow noise playbook B.

sec-analyst: Will open follow-ups: ENGSEC-321 (refine rule + deploy to prod after 24h staging observation), DASH-88 (dashboard panel for ci_session_burst), RUNBOOK-14 (add KMS fork). Assigning to ashish, olivia, marie respectively.

marie: sounds good — thanks team. :thumbsup:

ashish: i'll push a PR with the rule code and the exclusion list. expect it in ~30m.

olivia: monitoring panel added to staging workspace, will promote if staging looks clean. :eyes:

sec-analyst: closing thread for now. we will re-open if staging shows missed true positives.
